phoenix.subtitle: Conference City
phoenix.title: Phoenix, Arizona

intro.label: U.S. Southwest Hub
intro.desc: Located at the heart of Arizona in the U.S. Southwest, serving as the state capital and its political and economic center.

intro.label: Modern Desert Oasis
intro.desc: Nestled in the vast "Valley of the Sun" basin, surrounded by red-rock mountain ranges — the most vibrant metropolis in the Sonoran Desert.

intro.label: Seamless International Access
intro.desc: Adjacent to Phoenix Sky Harbor (PHX), just 10–15 minutes from the conference venue in Tempe — exceptionally convenient.

items.label: Semiconductor Cluster
items.desc: TSMC's Arizona fab is driving the entire supply chain into the region, with total investment expected to exceed $65 billion and a third advanced wafer fab planned for Phoenix. Intel, KoMiCo, Fujifilm, and other global giants continue to expand, forming a complete semiconductor ecosystem.

items.label: Emerging Technologies
items.desc: AI, autonomous vehicles (e.g., Joby Aviation's air taxi testing), and battery technology are becoming key new growth drivers.

items.label: Innovation Energy
items.desc: In 2026, Phoenix hosted the inaugural Arizona Tech Week and the Forbes 30 Under 30 Summit, showcasing its global competitiveness in entrepreneurship and advanced industries.

items.label: Core Pillars
items.desc: Beyond semiconductor manufacturing, financial services, healthcare, e-commerce logistics (as the Southwest's distribution hub), and tourism remain core economic pillars.

items.label: Global Connectivity
items.desc: In 2026, Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) launched its first direct flight to Asia, greatly enhancing business efficiency and international tourism appeal.

items.label: Jobs & Income
items.desc: The job market is expected to continue recovering in 2026, with personal income growth projected at 6.0%, demonstrating strong economic resilience.

categories.heading: Demographics & Lifestyle Upgrades
categories.tagline: A new benchmark for livable cities

items.label: Population Influx
items.desc: Continuous population migration is driving demand for residential and commercial space, with the 2026 real estate market expected to benefit from interest rate reductions.

items.label: Quality of Life
items.desc: With premium dining (e.g., Din Tai Fung) and major resort developments (e.g., VAI Resort), Phoenix is becoming a world-class culinary destination and high-quality living city.

items.label: Cost Advantage
items.desc: Compared to coastal cities, Phoenix maintains a relatively lower cost of living and excellent climate, attracting large numbers of professionals and families.

phoenix.outro: Phoenix is combining industrial strength, population growth, and comprehensive amenities to demonstrate a clear growth trajectory, securing a prominent position among U.S. cities.
